title: MZ Zooming In vs. Scaling Up for Pixelated Games

posts.author: JimFrom2003
posts.body:
What do you think is the best route to take if you want your game to have a low-resolution, "pixelated" visual style similar for RPG Maker 2000/2003 and other pixel games?
Is it better to actually reduce the game's resolution and use plugins to fit the new screen size, or to "cheat" by resizing the sprites so that it looks lower-res?

posts.author: Nirriti
posts.body:
For me, reducing the resolution is what looks best. But it might give you some headaches with font
(see

posts.author: KaijuuKimi
posts.body: Zoom keep everything true to the original. The caveat is newer software hate to use low resolution and always breaking the font, spacing and padding

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
I'm not a big fan of pixel, or rather retro-style games, but I wanted to give me 2 cents either way. I think if anything you should upscale your assets. There is also the possibility to use smaller tile sizes in MZ. I can not imagine picking up a game that comes with a 800x600 window size and actually play that.
Maybe that's cool for mobile? Or maybe if you have some way to hook it up to an old TV? But in the day and age where 4k screens are more and more common, I don't even want to imagine playing on a tiny window like that, let alone going full screen and watching what will result in pixel puke at best.
So, I guess my opinion is that pixel art is great, and it doesn't (Or shouldn't in my case) be restricted to a tiny window where I can't see jack.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I went for upscaled resources. Having 16x16 assets upscaled by 3 to 48x48 and make sure, they align strictly to the 3x3 grid, works best for me.
There have been several threads the past of people who applied a permanent zoom to their game (like working with 16x16 assets and scale the game up technically). At least that should be avoided. Having a permanent zoom will cause many compatibility issues in the long run you can't even think of yet.
Plugins, that can't handle it, menues being too big, text not readable, wrong interpretation of screen dimensions ...

This is why you scale your materials up, rather than trying to scale the rest of the game down.
The vast majority of RPG Maker users are most likely capable of scaling 8-or 16-bit style assets up by 300% in an image editor.
The vast majority of RPG Maker users are probably not capable of refactoring the code for every scene, window, and window-related sprite the engine provides in order to render them at a third of their default size.
Even if you wanted to for some reason to present your game at at 256x240px (or whatever—240p is roughly the resolution of the NES), most users are better off scaling up their materials, making minimal edits to the UI (or contracting them out within budget), and then using a plugin to scale the game window down to the target resolution.
